subject: Commercials: billing cadence, min-commit phasing & tax-residency mapping
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@calyx.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@calyx.com; michael.huang@calyx.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Initial redlines: billing flow + tax entity question

Hi Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and finance at Calyx reviewed the draft order form and sent a handful of redlines attached. High-level asks from our side:

- Can Redwood invoice into two legal entities across Q1/Q2 as we phase the product? (We need the first invoice to go to Calyx, Inc. and subsequent invoices to Calyx EU, s.r.o. once the regional entity is enabled.)
- We have a standard Net45 payment policy — can you confirm Redwood is okay with Net45 for this deal?
- Please confirm tax responsibility and whether Redwood can provide a tax residency certificate or VAT-proof evidence that Calyx EU will need for reclaim.

Attached: Calyx_Redline_Markup.docx with line-by-line comments. We tried to be conservative on commercial asks but need clarity on invoice routing and min-commit phasing: we propose a three-tranche min-commit (30%/40%/30%).

Goal: finalize the order form so legal can approve and procurement can issue the PO by next Thursday (Jan 28). Can you loop in your finance/legal folks and share a short plan?

Thanks —
Sarah Li
Sr. Procurement Manager | Calyx Systems
[Attachment: Calyx_Redline_Markup.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@calyx.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: billing flow + tax entity question

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear summary and the marked-up doc. Looping in Lauren (finance) and Ben (sales) to validate feasibility. Quick notes from my side:

- Invoice entity mapping: we can support split invoicing (different entities per tranche) but need legal-approved order form language and signed SOW that lists the entity mapping and effective dates.
- Net45: acceptable, but finance will confirm whether we require any payment guarantee for the first tranche.
- Tax evidence: Redwood can provide a tax residency statement and our W-8 / VAT evidence. Lauren, can you confirm what package we can share?

Proposed internal next steps:
1) Finance (Lauren) reviews and confirms the exact wording for invoice routing and any PO requirements.
2) Legal to accept the entity-split language in an amendment to the order form (we'll provide redline).
3) Sales (Ben) to confirm commercial acceptance of the 30/40/30 phasing or propose an alternate that preserves ARR recognition timing.

I attached the latest Order Form (v3) for reference — includes the current payment schedule slots we usually use.

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Calyx_OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: billing flow + tax entity question

Thanks for the loop, Connor. I reviewed Calyx's redlines and here's what finance can offer:

- Invoice routing: finance can accept up to two invoice entities with clearly defined effective dates. We'll need Calyx to include the entity legal name, tax ID, and remit-to address in the PO.
- Tax documentation: we can provide a Redwood VAT certificate plus our global tax residency letter. I'll attach our standard Tax_Cert_Reqs.xlsx which lists acceptable documents and formats. Calyx will still be responsible for any local withholding or VAT where applicable — we can include the VAT clause in the order form appendix.
- Net terms: Net45 is fine for this customer class, provided the first tranche is invoiced to Calyx, Inc. with a PO and there is no outstanding credit hold. For larger first-tranche amounts we typically ask for a billing contact and an invoice acceptance window (10 business days) to avoid disputes delaying recognition.

Contract redline suggestions (legal will need to incorporate):
1) Payment Schedule table: specify Tranche 1 (effective date + entity A), Tranche 2 (date or usage milestone + entity B), Tranche 3 (final billing).
2) Invoicing section: require PO number on invoice and remit-to per-entity.
3) Taxes: add clause that customer is responsible for local indirect taxes; Redwood to provide residency/withholding documentation on request.

Attached: Tax_Cert_Reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet) with formats and examples.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Tax_Cert_Reqs.xlsx (XLSX, 26KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com; lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: billing flow + tax entity question

Quick commercial take —

- 30/40/30 phasing is doable but we'd like to protect Redwood's cash profile. Can we propose the following compromise: 25% upfront (upon signature), 50% at the regional entity cutover or 6 months in (whichever comes first), 25% at contract anniversary? This reduces our exposure while keeping most of Calyx's requested phasing.
- On Net45: okay to accept, but ask for a Customer Success milestone (activation acceptance) before invoicing Tranche 2 to reduce disputes.
- Legal redlines: I'll draft a concise amendment focusing only on invoice entity mapping and payment schedule — keep the rest of the order form as-is to speed sign.

Connor — if you can get Calyx to confirm entity legal names and PO timing we can prepare the amendment and get legal to fast-track. I can also offer a one-time onboarding credit if they sign within the procurement timeline Sarah set (by Jan 28).

Ben
Principal Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@calyx.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com; ben.carter@redwood.com; michael.huang@calyx.com
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redlines: billing flow + tax entity question

Sarah —

Thanks — good progress. Summary and proposed next steps from Redwood:

- Invoice entity mapping: Redwood can accept split invoicing across two legal entities. Please confirm the legal name, tax ID, and remit-to address for both entities in your PO.
- Payment phasing: Redwood proposes (25% upfront / 50% mid-phase / 25% year-end) as a compromise to preserve cash and accelerate legal acceptance. If Calyx prefers the 30/40/30 we can escalate but it may require additional finance approvals.
- Net terms: Net45 is acceptable. For Tranche 2 we request a CS activation acceptance window (10 business days) before invoice issuance.
- Tax docs: Lauren will send the Redwood tax residency letter and our standard evidence pack; Calyx should send any local VAT registration to coordinate reclaim.

Action items:
1) Calyx (Sarah/Michael) to confirm entity legal names, tax IDs, and remit addresses by EOD Jan 21.
2) Redwood (Connor/Ben) to prepare a limited amendment to the Order Form reflecting the invoice entity mapping and payment schedule; legal to review and return by Jan 24.
3) Calyx procurement to provide PO once amendment language is confirmed; Redwood to prepare DocuSign envelope.

I attached the edited Order Form and will circulate the amendment draft once Ben finalizes. If Calyx is comfortable with the compromise phasing we can hit procurement's PO target.

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Calyx_OrderForm_v3.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]
[Attachment: DocuSign_Envelope_98765.link (LINK)]
